Drive towards meetings that position Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) as the execution layer for AIOps- Turning AI insights into automated action Resources : Webinar: Scale your AI: Automation strategies for infrastructure and AIOps Ebook: Unlock the full potential of AIOps with automation Checklist: 5 practical AIOps use cases Webinar: AIOps Told You What's Wrong. Hi {{first_name}}, Most teams have invested in AIOps and monitoring platforms. They detect issues faster — but remediation still takes time. That gap between detection and resolution is where MTTR expands and engineering hours disappear. Organizations are closing that gap by connecting AIOps insights directly to automated remediation with Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform — turning alerts into standardized, governed action across hybrid environments. Instead of notifying engineers, the system can: Auto-resolve common incidents Enrich tickets with context Remediate drift before it spreads If improving MTTR without increasing headcount is a priority, is this worth a 20-minute discussion? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Email #2 - Alert Fatigue  , Slow Response Subject: Alert fatigue slowing down your team? Hi {{first_name}}, Curious if this sounds familiar for you and your team: Alert noise without clear signal on what actually requires action Incidents escalating across teams despite investments in monitoring and AIOps The same issues recurring because insights aren’t connected to automated resolution. Many teams tell us that they are generating more insights than ever, but still rely on manual steps to resolve issues. Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform is helping close that gap by automating the repetitive, predictable parts of incident response -  especially for common, high-volume issues that drain time. Can we speak Wednesday or Thursday of next week to see if automation potentially could reduce MTTR? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Email #3 - Tech Debt , Inconsistent Ops Subject: The hidden cost of repetitive incidents Hi {{first_name}}, A pattern we’re seeing: a lot of the operational cost in IT isn’t from major incidents -  it’s from the constant, repetitive fixes and triage that teams handle manually. Over time, that becomes tech debt and results in slower delivery and unnecessary outages. Teams are addressing this by connecting their AIOps tools directly to automation with Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform That shift provides: Automated resolution of repetitive incidents to reduce manual effort Standardized, consistent remediation across environments Faster response with fewer errors without adding headcount I can walk through how other organizations are doing this and where it typically delivers the fastest wins. Can we find some time this week or next? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Email #4 - MTTR, Risk, Compliance (for Executives) Subject: Where teams are cutting MTTR without adding headcount Hi {{first_name}}, One theme from IT leaders lately: They're spending more time responding to incidents than preventing them. Even with strong AIOps tools, most teams still rely on manual remediation, which slows response time and increases operational risk. By combining AIOps with Ansible Automation Platform, teams are: Reducing MTTR significantly Eliminating drift-related outages Enforcing compliance automatically Improving resilience across environments It’s one of the few levers that improves reliability and reduces cost at the same time. If this aligns with what you’re working on, l et's connect next week. Would Tuesday or Thursday work for your schedule? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Email #5 - Proof Point, Ecosystem Subject: What customers are achieving with AIOps + Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform Hi {{first_name}}, A quick example: A customer recently connected their AIOps platform with Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform to auto-remediate the top recurring incidents, significantly reducing service downtime. They cut resolution time by 50% and eliminated thousands of manual tickets. Rather than replacing existing tools, Ansible Automation Platform integrates with observability platforms like Instana, Splunk, Dynatrace, LogicMonitor, and ServiceNow - turning insights from multiple sources into coordinated automated actions that fix drift, resolve config issues, and address performance problems before they impact users. If you're looking to see real results from your AIOps investments, I can share what leading organizations are doing today. Would {{time_option}} work for a short conversation? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Conversation Starters: “How actionable are the insights coming out of your AIOps or monitoring tools today?” “What slows down response time the most once an issue is detected?” “Where do repetitive incidents consume the most time for your team?” “How often does configuration drift or misconfigurations cause problems?” “Do you have any automated remediation in place right now?” “How much time would your team save if 20–30% of incidents resolved themselves?” “Which tools are creating the most noise or alert fatigue?” “Do tickets come enriched with enough context for quick resolution?” “How consistent is the remediation process across your environments?” “Where do you see the biggest opportunity to reduce MTTR?” Additional Questions By Persona: IT Operations Leader/Director of IT Operations Use these to deepen discovery and tie AIOps → Action → Automation → MTTR reduction. Operational Efficiency “Which incidents or issues consume most of your operations time today?” “How long does it typically take to go from alert → diagnosis → fix?” “Where do manual steps slow things down the most?” AIOps + Observability Gaps “Are insights from your AIOps or monitoring tools actionable today?” “Do alerts come with enough context for your team to respond quickly?” “Which alerts would you automate first if you could?” Repetition + Process Consistency “Which problems does your team end up fixing more than once?” “How consistent is your remediation process across environments?” Risk + Drift “How often does configuration drift cause issues or outages?” “Do you have automated checks or enforcement for drift today?” Team Capacity “If repetitive incidents disappeared tomorrow, what would your team finally have time to focus on?” “Are you under pressure to improve MTTR without adding headcount?”

Automation Architect, Engineer / Sys Admin Email #1 Subject: What you know about AWX and Ansible Tower is wrong Hi {{first_name}}, Question: Are AWX, Ansible Tower, and Ansible Automation Platform essentially the same thing? Answer: No AWX = An unsupported collection of open source projects intended for testing and development only. Ansible Tower = A previous Red Hat solution that was last made generally available in 2019. Ansible Automation Platform = A full suite of enterprise-grade features that are supported and designed for ease of use and scale, including: Generative AI to help you manage and troubleshoot your automation and generate automation code fast. Automation analytics to help you measure and track your automation ROI, time savings, and performance. Self-service automation to help you extend automation to more users without sacrificing control. Event-driven automation to proactively respond to adverse events in your IT operations. Policy enforcement to help you maintain compliance and governance in an AIOps world. Ansible Automation Platform has a suite of new features that are worth a closer look. Are you available for a brief call next week to discuss? Best regards, {{sender.first_name}} Email #2 Subject: 7 reasons why your IT automation is failing Hi {{first_name}}, This is {{sender.first_name}} from your extended team at Red Hat. I want to share the most common reasons we see too many organizations like yours fail to achieve their desired results with IT automation: Lack of executive sponsorship, strategy and roadmap for IT automation Inconsistent standards, governance, and tooling across teams Inability to execute cross-domain workflows that drive efficiency No formal measurement of automation ROI, time savings, etc. Too much control over automation given to a single team or individuals Resistance to change in tools and/or processes Maintenance of DIY tools like AWX that stifle productivity and innovation Can we set up a time to explore how Ansible Automation Platform and Red Hat can help you overcome these obstacles to innovation? Best regards, {{sender.first_name}} Email #3 Subject: Your IT automation is stealing your time Hi {{first_name}}, If you're using AWX to run your enterprise automation, you're spending time on management and maintenance that could be redirected towards innovation projects that drive your business forward–as opposed to just keeping the lights on. At Red Hat, we see time and time again that organizations that adopt the right solutions and approaches to automation are more productive, agile, and performative than their counterparts–and typically with lower TCO. Can we set up a time for me to share examples of organizations around the world who are automating at scale with success? Looking forward to your response! {{sender.first_name}} Conversation Starters: What is your automation strategy? How do you ensure teams are acting in alignment with that strategy? Are you able to use a single unified tool to automate across multiple domains? Have you begun thinking about how your team will prepare for AI? What is in your plan so far? What’s getting in the way of you and an ideal, automated infrastructure? What are your top IT challenges? How do you measure automation performance? How are teams aligned? Are they collaborating or do they operate in silos? Are you using any free or community-based automation tools? How many automation tools are in use across all of IT? Are you still relying on manual scripting for patching and provisioning?

Subject Line: Streamline your NetOps processes Hi {{first_name}}, As network operations expand in scope, it is becoming more challenging to manage networks across hybrid cloud environments. To keep up with complex tasks that span from data centers to edge locations, network teams must turn to automated NetOps. Here are a few resources that show how organizations are using Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform to orchestrate workflows across network and other domains for more efficient, resilient operations: Network automation guide for Ansible Automation Platform Checklist: 5 practical AIOps use cases 5 great use cases for Network Automation Let me know if you’d like to schedule a brief chat to see how we can help your organization. How does next {{weekdays_from_now 2}} or {{weekdays_from_now 3}} work for you? Thank you, {{sender.first_name}} Email #2 Subject: The bigger picture - seeing real ROI from your automation investments Hi {{first_name}}, IT leaders are now asking their teams to show clearer ROI on their automation investments - especially as budgets get tighter. With Red Hat’s Ansible Automation platform, we can help teams: Automate network device configuration and management Apply consistent governance and security policies across your infrastructure Orchestrate complex workflows that span multiple domains (e.g., network, security, and cloud) I thought you might appreciate this , which details the financial benefits and business value our customers have seen. It is not about doing more - it's about getting more value from your automation. Can we schedule 15 minutes to discuss how we help teams position this for leadership consideration? {{sender.first_name}} Email #3 Subject: {{sender.first_name}}, how are you supporting your NetOps teams? {{first_name}}, How are you supporting the needs of rapidly shifting workload requirements for your business? Are your network teams keeping up with the demands of modern digital infrastructure? Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform can be used to automate entire network and IT processes across devices and domains - no matter if you are starting from scratch or scaling out. With automated NetOps, network engineers can use a variety of automation techniques to perform management and maintenance tasks, as well as respond automatically when conditions change across a network. Lets sync for 15 minutes to see how this could look in your organization, how does next {{weekdays_from_now 2}} look? Best, {{sender.first_name}} Conversation Starters: If you’re nice and have extra brain power, a few conversation starters would be appreciated. Are you still relying on manual scripting for patching and provisioning?

How to pitch Inference at Scale
Inference at Scale Sales Tactic Intro Video

The Inference at Scale Sales Tactic is all about offering customers the opportunity to achieve more with less. Get more of out every GPU and entire infrastructure. Watch this 4-minute video to learn how you can help customers serve more users and agents efficiently and cost-effectively.
Why Inference at Scale?
Fast, cost-effective AI inference with Red Hat AI Inference Server

Struggling to deploy increasingly complex AI models efficiently and affordably? Red Hat® AI Inference Server is engineered to help your organization overcome these critical deployment hurdles at scale. Join Michael Goin, Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat, as he explains how Red Hat is paving the way for more accessible and impactful AI. Discover how your enterprise can achieve: ✅ Consistent Performance: Ensure reliable results and high-speed processing for your most demanding AI applications and large language models (LLMs). ✅ Fast Deployment Cycles: Accelerate your time-to-value with access to validated, pre-optimized generative AI models ready for production. ✅ Cost-Effective Operations: Significantly reduce the operational costs typically associated with running inference for complex AI workloads. Powered by cutting-edge open source technologies like vLLM at its core, and featuring advanced model optimization capabilities (including LLM Compressor), Red Hat AI Inference Server offers unparalleled flexibility. Run your AI inference workloads wherever you need them—from your datacenter, to the public cloud, and out to the edge—all while maintaining accuracy and efficiency. It's time to make your AI innovation sustainable, scalable, and a true competitive advantage.
